messages.body_plain:
>From personal use and helping students, I have found 90% of crashes in Rstudio are because of Rstudio. R is pretty difficult to crash outright. I can count on one hand the times I have completely crashed R running through Emacs, and half of those were definitely my fault. Rstudio seems to crash all the time.

On Wednesday, January 31, 2018 at 12:52:20 PM UTC-8, Alex Mandel wrote:
> As a note on that. I have found that running scripts with Rscript on
> command line is more stable for large analysis than in Rstudio, even on
> a very big machine. More likely to crash with a message too, rather than
> hang, since the error does not need to get passed back to Rstudio. I'm
> guessing your R session crashed in a way that didn't report back to Rstudio.
>
> Enjoy,
>
> Alex Mandel, PhD
>
> Center for Spatial Sciences
>   http://spatial.ucdavis.edu
> Geospatial and Farming Systems Research Consortium
>   http://gfc.ucdavis.edu
> University of California, Davis

messages.subject: nested ANOVA for grouping factor
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I do appreciate if someone kindly help me that enables me to perform nested design ANOVA on my data.

I did linear regression (six models) between two variables (LnB and LnC) and also I added catgorial variables as a grouping factor (six group factors, site, vegetation type, Topography, soil texture, direction, disturbance) in each model, as following:

data <- read_excel("C:/Users/Anvar/Documents/multispecies.xlsx",sheet=1)

data$disturbance <- factor(data$disturbance)

data$site <- factor(data$site)

data$vegtype <- factor(data$vegtype)

data$Direction <- factor(data$Direction)

data$Texture <- factor(data$Texture)

data$Topo <- factor(data$Topo)

#####################  multispecies analysis, Models using only C

lm1 <- lm(LnB ~ LnC+ disturbance, data=data)
summary(lm1)

lm2 <- lm(LnB ~ LnC+ Direction, data=data)
summary(lm2)

lm3 <- lm(LnB ~ LnC+vegtype, data=data)
summary(lm3)

lm4 <- lm(LnB ~ LnC+ Topo, data=data)
summary(lm4)

lm5 <- lm(LnB ~ LnC+Texture, data=data)
summary(lm5)

lm6 <- lm(LnB ~ LnC+ site, data=data)
summary(lm6)

now I want to do nested analysis variance (ANOVA) for finding that how much of the relative residual variance (%) is explained by each group factor.

Thanks for the help in advance.
Best Regards,
Anvar,

messages.subject: [D-RUG]: Michael Culshaw-Maurer talk on optimization planning next week
messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: Michael Culshaw-Maurer talk on optimization planning next week
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUG Folks,

Next Monday, Michael Culshaw-Maurer will be presenting his talk at Davis R Users Group (Sheilds Library Rm 360) on planning for optimization and premature optimization with a talk entitled "Avoiding the R-oot of All Evil: Premature Optimization".  Here is a little blurb from Michael:

Have you ever wished your code ran faster? Have you ever come back from an extended coffee break to find your model still running? Have you ever come close to putting your fist through your computer when your advisor asked why your data weren't analyzed yet? Well, you're not alone. This talk will go through some tools and methods to make sure you have a plan before jumping into optimization willy nilly. I can't promise your models will run faster, but I can promise there will be lots of bad puns and a few cool methods.

Michael will be starting his talk at 10:00, and will finish up by 11, so there will be plenty of time for questions! Hope to see you all there!

Best,
Martha (one of the new D-RUG coordinators)

--
Martha Wohlfeil

Graduate Group in Ecology
Avian Ecology Lab, Doctoral Student
Wickson Hall 3017
University of California, Davis

messages.subject: Welcoming new D-RUG Co-Coordinators!
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGies!

D-RUG was started around fall of 2012 and now has 898 members. Thanks to everyone who has participating in one way or another. This group has been an amazing and supportive community for so many, and in order to keep it going it's important to have folks willing to maintain and organize our weekly meeting, maintain the website, and arrange for a presentation or two.

So, I wanted to introduce and welcome two new co-coordinators to D-RUG!

Taylor Reiter and Martha Wohlfeil have kindly volunteered to help co-coordinate, so please keep your eyes peeled for future emails/communication from them. They are both awesome and have been consistent participants and helpers at the weekly D-RUG meetings.

Taylor is a 2nd year graduate student in the Food Science graduate group at UC Davis. She studies how microbes survive in and change the metabolite profile of olive oil. She has experience wrangling genomic data, building websites, and using git in R.

Martha is a 2nd year graduate student in the ecology department at UC Davis. She studies avian biogeography in the Great Basin and has experience building statistical models and working with mapping software.

Thanks and hope to see some of you on Mondays!

Adios,
Ryan

(now just one of the Co-coordinators of D-RUG!)

--

"When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the universe."
John Muir (My First Summer in the Sierra, 1911)
-----------------------------------------------------

PhD Candidate, Graduate Group in Ecology
Center for Watershed Sciences, UC Davis

@riverpeek

messages.subject: Michele Tobias' DSI workshop this Friday: Projections for Spatial Data
messages.subject_clean: Michele Tobias' DSI workshop this Friday: Projections for Spatial Data
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Happy Presidents Day! I wanted to let everyone know about a DSI workshop <http://dsi.ucdavis.edu/posts/Workshop/Projection20180223.html> happening later this week by Michele Tobias (the University Library's GIS curator) entitled "Projections for Spatial Data in R." The workshop will be on Friday, Feb. 23rd from 9:30-12 in 360 Shields Library, please register with this <https://forms.library.ucdavis.edu/classes/register.php?classid=2295> link.

Here's a quick description of the workshop:

If you’ve ever worked with spatial data, you’ve had one of those moments – two datasets that are for the same geographic location show up in two different countries in a map or you run a spatial analysis process and come up with an empty result. Why? The answer often has to do with projections. In this workshop, we’ll clarify some of the mysteries of working with projections and discuss how to avoid common mistakes. For hands-on experience, we’ll work with R, but the concepts will apply to any GIS tool or spatial database.

Have a great day off, and hope to see you all there!

Best,

Martha (one of the D-RUG coordinators)

# Announcing the 2018 Data Intensive Biology Summer Institute (DIBSI)!

Link: http://ivory.idyll.org/dibsi/

Where: Davis, California; in Valley Hall at UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine
When: June 25 to July 14, 2018 (multiple events; see below)
What: Computational training for research-active biologists and bioinformaticians!
Contact info: please send questions to [dibsi.t...@gmail.com](mailto:dib...@gmail.com).

This summer, the Lab for Data Intensive Biology will host a summer institute for biologists interested in learning or improving upon computational skills. This will include a two week no-skills-required workshop (July 2-July 14) during which biologists will learn cloud computing, UNIX command line skills, and high-throughput shotgun sequencing data analysis -- this workshop was successfully run for seven years at Michigan State University and moved to UC Davis last year.

DIBSI is open to anyone and everyone.

The activities at the DIBSI will include:

* A two-day instructor training course for teachers and core facility personnel to become Carpentry instructors (June 25-26);
* Several Software and Data Carpentry 2-day workshops (June 27-28);
* A two-week introductory bioinformatics workshop ([see materials from 2017](https://angus.readthedocs.io/en/2017)) (July 2-July 14)

All materials from the workshops will be freely and openly available for reuse after the Summer Institute.

For more information, please see the DIBSI 2018 Web site at http://ivory.idyll.org/dibsi/.

Applications for ANGUS are open until Mar 5!: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeuXw5aX6NUGdzb4NnhQi3CLEMIxHr_vvVZFB762fCJkkkYGA/viewform - after that, acceptance will be on a rolling basis given availability.
